red_flags.evidence: locked immediately click http://bit.ly/kyc-upd8 and updat
red_flags.why: The message pushes you to a link. Genuine banks do not send KYC or bill links on SMS. Shortened and cheap domains (.top, .xyz) are used to hide the real website.

red_flags.evidence: day your account will be blocked immediately click http:/
red_flags.why: Fear and a deadline is the oldest trick in the book. Real institutions send written notice and give you time - they never threaten instant blocking in a text message.

red_flags.evidence: mer your KYC is expiring today your account will be blo
red_flags.why: Manufactured urgency stops you from thinking or checking with someone. Slow down - that alone defeats most of these attacks.

red_flags.evidence: Dear customer your KYC is expiring today your a
red_flags.why: The sender is copying a trusted name to borrow its authority. Check the actual sender ID and contact the institution on the number printed on your card or bill.

red_flags.evidence: t.ly/kyc-upd8 and update pan card details
red_flags.why: Your ID numbers and card photos are enough to open accounts and loans in your name. They are never needed over SMS or WhatsApp.

reasoning_trace: Model scored the message at 95.9% fraud probability.
Agent matched 5 of 10 known fraud red-flag rules.
Strongest signals: Suspicious link, Account / service threat, Urgency pressure.
next_steps: Do not click any link, do not scan any QR code, and do not reply to the message.
Do not share the OTP, PIN, CVV or password with anyone - not even someone claiming to be bank staff.
Verify on your own: open the bank's official app or call the number printed on your card / bill.
If money has already left your account, call the national cyber crime helpline 1930 immediately - the first 24 hours matter most.
Report the message at cybercrime.gov.in and forward it to 1909 to report the sender.
Tell one other person - a parent, neighbour or colleague - what this message looked like.
